files.lesson.md: --- order: 3 unit: expressions node: AC9M7A01 n3 assumes: [AC9M5A01 n3] title: Finding an unknown summary: When a formula's answer is known but one letter is not, substitute what you know. That leaves an equation; solve it by undoing, then check. language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "You know how much fence you have and how long the garden bed must be. How wide can it be?" connection: hire-hours # data/connections/maths.yml (Make on paper and Also used in; documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8144 url: http://127.0.0.1:8144/index.html readySelector: "#sl-w" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: formula.yml#pic, caption: "$P = 20$ and $l = 6$: $20 = 2 \\times 6 + 2w$, so $2w = 8$ and $w = 4$. Check: $2 \\times 6 + 2 \\times 4 = 20$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@formula.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Substitute what you know, then solve for the rest" say: "Substitute what you know, then solve for the letter you don't." clip: - caption: { text: "P = 20 cm and l = 6 cm. What is w?", say: "The perimeter is twenty and the length is six. What is the width?" } - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "20 = 2 × 6 + 2w, so 20 = 12 + 2w.", say: "Twenty equals twelve plus two w." } - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "Undo + 12: 2w = 8. Undo × 2: w = 4.", say: "Take away twelve: two w is eight. Divide by two: w is four." } - click: Make w bigger - click: Make w bigger - click: Make w bigger - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "Check: 2 × 6 + 2 × 4 = 20.", say: "Check it: two times six plus two times four is twenty." } - expect: { selector: ".rulework", contains: "P = 2 × 6 + 2 × 4 = 20" } - wait: 1200 --- So far you knew the letters and worked out the answer. Sometimes you know the answer, and one letter is the **unknown**. ## Predict: how wide? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a width exposes subtracting the length once instead of twice, and forgetting to halve." check: type: predict q: "A rectangle has perimeter $P = 20$ cm and length $l = 6$ cm. Using $P = 2l + 2w$, what is its width $w$?" options: ["4", "8", "14", "7"] actual: "4. 20 = 2 × 6 + 2w, so 20 = 12 + 2w. Then 2w = 8 and w = 4. (8 forgets to halve; 14 takes the length away only once.)" ``` $$P = 2l + 2w$$ Which letters do you know? Which one is unknown? ## Run: find the width ```step stage: run insight: "Moving w until P reaches 20 shows the answer; the working shows why only one width fits." try: { playground: board, starter: "formula.yml#run", height: 520 } check: { type: board, text: "Keep $l = 6$. Change $w$ until the perimeter is 20 cm. Was your prediction right?", when: "P = 20 and l = 6" } ``` Change $w$ one step at a time. How much does $P$ go up for each 1 cm of width? Why? When you know the answer and one letter is missing, substitute what you know. What is left is an equation, and you can solve it by undoing, as in the Equations unit. ## Investigate: substitute, then solve ```step stage: investigate insight: "Substituting the known values turns a formula into an equation with one unknown; solving undoes the operations in reverse order; the check substitutes back." tasks: - picture: { ref: formula.yml#pic, caption: "The rectangle with $P = 20$ and $l = 6$: the width is 4." } check: type: answer q: "A rectangle has area $A = 24$ cm² and length $l = 6$ cm. Using $A = lw$, find its width $w$." answer: "4" feedback: - ["144", "24 = 6 × w. To undo × 6, divide by 6."] - ["18", "That takes 6 away. lw means l × w: undo × by dividing."] explain: "24 = 6w, so w = 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Check: 6 × 4 = 24." - check: type: answer q: "A plumber charges $C = 5h + 20$ dollars. A job cost 45 dollars. How many hours, $h$?" answer: "5" feedback: - ["245", "That puts 45 in as h. Here 45 is the cost C: 45 = 5h + 20."] - ["13", "Undo the + 20 first (take 20 away), then divide by 5."] - ["9", "45 ÷ 5 = 9 skips the call-out fee. Take 20 away first."] explain: "45 = 5h + 20, so 5h = 25 and h = 5. Check: 5 × 5 + 20 = 45." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia finds the width of a rectangle. Click the line where she goes wrong." answer: 5 fault: logic misconception: undo-same-operation explain: "Line 5: 2w = 8 means 2 × w = 8. To undo × 2, divide by 2: w = 4. Mia multiplied again. Check: 2 × 6 + 2 × 16 = 44, not 20." ``` ### Area Here is how to find an unknown in a formula. ```worked P = 2l + 2w :: Write the formula. P = 20, \; l = 6 :: Write what you know. The unknown is $w$. 20 = 2 \times 6 + 2w :: Substitute. Now it is an equation with one unknown. 20 = 12 + 2w :: Work out what you can. 8 = 2w :: Undo the + 12: take 12 from both sides. w = 4 :: Undo the × 2: divide both sides by 2. 2 \times 6 + 2 \times 4 = 20 \;\checkmark :: Check by substituting back into the formula. ``` ### A plumber ### Find the mistake Read Mia's working one line at a time. Does her answer check? ## Modify: other unknowns ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a decimal answer, a different letter unknown, a formula that subtracts, and three letters with one unknown." try: { playground: board, starter: "formula.yml#drive", height: 420 } tasks: - starter: "formula.yml#drive" hint: "150 = 60t. Undo × 60." check: { type: board, text: "A car travels at 60 km/h: $d = 60t$. How long does it take to go 150 km? Set $t$ to find out.", when: "d = 150", explain: "150 = 60t, so t = 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours." } - starter: "formula.yml#area" hint: "30 = l × 5. Undo × 5." check: { type: board, text: "A rectangle is 5 cm wide with an area of 30 cm². Keep $w = 5$ and find its length.", when: "A = 30 and w = 5", explain: "30 = 5l, so l = 6." } - starter: "formula.yml#battery" hint: ["60 = 100 − 4m. How much charge has been used?", "40 has been used, at 4 a minute."] check: { type: board, text: "A phone battery has $B = 100 - 4m$ percent left after $m$ minutes of gaming. When is it at 60%?", when: "B = 60", explain: "60 = 100 − 4m, so 4m = 40 and m = 10 minutes." } - check: type: answer q: "A box has volume $V = lwh$. $V = 60$, $l = 5$ and $w = 3$. Find $h$." answer: "4" feedback: - ["900", "60 = 5 × 3 × h = 15h. Undo × 15 by dividing."] - ["52", "lwh means multiply. 5 × 3 = 15, so 60 = 15h."] explain: "60 = 5 × 3 × h = 15h, so h = 60 ÷ 15 = 4. Check: 5 × 3 × 4 = 60." ``` ### A car trip Each task loads a new formula. Write the equation first, solve it, then set the board to check. ### A different unknown ### Going down ### A box ## Practise: find the unknown ```step stage: practise insight: "Substituting and solving in new formulas, mixed with one plain substitution so students must decide which job each question needs; the review is from the Equations unit." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Concert tickets cost $T = 12n + 6$ dollars. An order cost 66 dollars. How many tickets?" answer: "5" feedback: - ["798", "66 is the total T, not n: 66 = 12n + 6."] - ["6", "Take away the 6 first: 12n = 60."] explain: "66 = 12n + 6, so 12n = 60 and n = 5." - check: type: answer q: "Using $T = 12n + 6$, what do 3 tickets cost?" answer: "42" feedback: - ["0.25", "Here n is known (3), so substitute: no solving needed."] explain: "T = 12 × 3 + 6 = 42 dollars. Here you know n, so you just substitute." - check: type: answer q: "Average speed is $s = d / t$. A cyclist rides at 20 km/h for $t = 3$ hours. How far, $d$, in km?" answer: "60" feedback: - ["6.67", "20 = d ÷ 3. To undo ÷ 3, multiply by 3."] explain: "20 = d ÷ 3, so d = 20 × 3 = 60 km." - check: type: answer q: "Review: solve $4x - 3 = 17$." answer: "5" feedback: - ["3.5", "Undo the − 3 first by adding 3, then divide by 4."] explain: "4x = 20, so x = 5. Check: 4 × 5 − 3 = 17." ``` ### Tickets ### Substitute or solve? ### A bike ride ### Review ## Make: a garden bed ```step stage: make insight: "Meeting two conditions at once (a fixed perimeter and a shape rule) reverses the lesson: the student chooses the unknowns." try: { playground: board, starter: "formula.yml#make", height: 520 } hint: ["The length is twice the width: P = 2(2w) + 2w = 6w.", "6w = 24. What is w?"] check: { type: board, text: "You have 24 m of edging for a garden bed. Make the length twice the width, using all 24 m.", when: "P = 24 and l = 2w", explain: "l = 8 and w = 4: 2 × 8 + 2 × 4 = 24, and 8 is twice 4." } ``` The bed must use exactly 24 m of edging, and be twice as long as it is wide. Stretch: with the same 24 m, which rectangle gives the biggest area? ## Make: kayak hire on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A hire price is a formula with a known total and an unknown number of hours; the paper task asks which letter the known number replaces." hint: ["The money you have is the total cost.", "Undo the fee first, then divide."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Kayak hire costs $T = 5n + 8$ dollars for $n$ hours. You have \\$43. On paper, put the known value into the formula, solve for $n$ and check." steps: - ["$43 = 5n + 8$", "T is the total cost, so 43 goes in for T"] - ["$43 - 8 = 35$, so $5n = 35$", "undo the + 8 first"] - ["$n = 35 \\div 5 = 7$", "then undo the × 5"] - ["Check: $5 \\times 7 + 8 = 35 + 8 = 43$", "put 7 back into the formula"] picks: - step: 1 q: "Why does 43 go in for $T$?" options: - "$T$ is the total cost, and \\$43 is the money available" - "43 is the number we do not know, so it goes in for $n$" - "43 and 8 are both money, so they are added" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "$n$ is the unknown. The 43 is the known total, so it replaces $T$.", "Substitute 43 for $T$ and keep the 8 in the formula."] answer: "7" answerLabel: "Hours" feedback: - ["0.6", "That divides 43 by 5 first. Undo the + 8 first."] - ["35", "That is $5n$. Divide by 5 to find the hours."] criteria: - "I put 43 in for T and left n as the unknown." - "I undid the + 8 before the × 5." - "I checked 7 hours in the formula." explain: "43 = 5n + 8, so 5n = 35 and n = 7 hours. Check: 5 × 7 + 8 = 43." ``` Do this one in your book. The prices are made up, but hire shops charge a fee plus a rate like this. Write each step, check by substituting 7, then type the hours and choose the reason for the first line. **Also used in** - **Hire prices.** Bike hire is a fixed fee plus a rate per hour: with \$30, how many hours can you afford? - **Speed and distance.** $d = st$ with $d$ and $s$ known gives an equation for $t$. - **Next lessons.** The Equations unit, and finding $x$ for a given $y$ on a graph in Linear relations. ```teacher summary: Students substitute the known values into a formula, solve the equation that is left for the unknown, and check by substituting back (AC9M7A01, node 3). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can substitute the values I know into a formula to make an equation. - I can solve the equation by undoing each operation, last first. - I can check my answer by substituting it back into the formula. struggle: Choosing which letter the known number belongs to, then undoing the operation rather than repeating it. Write each known value beside its letter before substituting, and check by substituting back every time. before: > Do the Run and Modify boards yourself first. The board lets students hunt for the answer by moving a slider: that is fine at Run, but in Investigate and Modify they should write the equation and solve it first, then use the board to check. The new move is putting together substitution (last lesson) and backtracking (Equations unit). The common error is repeating the operation instead of undoing it (Mia's mistake: 2w = 8, so w = 16). The check catches it every time, so make checking non-negotiable. One practise question needs only substitution, on purpose: students must decide which job each question asks for. running: - "Predict: ask students who chose 14 or 8 to check their width in P = 2l + 2w." - "Run: ask why P goes up 2 for each 1 cm of width." - "Investigate: model the worked example live. Ask after each line: what did we undo?" - "Modify: for the battery, ask what the minus means before anyone calculates." - "Make: ask how they found it: guessing with the slider, or writing 6w = 24?" - "Paper: kayak hire is worked in books (substitute, undo the fee, divide, check). The page marks 7 and the reason 43 replaces T. Books out, then look at the page for the model." stuck: - see: A student repeats the operation instead of undoing it (Mia's mistake). ask: Does your answer check? Put it back into the formula. fix: Undo × with ÷, and + with −. Check every answer by substituting back. - see: A student puts the known answer in for the wrong letter (45 as h). ask: Which letter is the cost? Which is the hours? fix: Write each known value next to its letter before substituting. stretch: A rectangle's length is 3 cm more than its width, and its perimeter is 30 cm. Find both sides. support: "Give a template: formula; what I know; substitute; undo; check." leads: > Next: the Expressions unit continues with writing expressions from words. Solving for an unknown is the Equations unit, and in Linear relations it becomes finding x for a given y on a graph. exit: q: A gym costs T = 15w + 30 dollars for w weeks. Someone paid 120 dollars. How many weeks? Check your answer. a: "120 = 15w + 30, so 15w = 90 and w = 6. Check: 15 × 6 + 30 = 120." explain: > When you know a formula's answer but not one of its letters, **substitute** the values you know. What is left is an **equation** with one unknown. Solve it by **undoing**: undo the last operation first (+ and − before × and ÷). Then **check**: put your answer back into the formula. It should give the value you started with. ```
